title: Why Johnny Adopts Identity-Based Software Signing: A Usability Case Study of Sigstore
review_status: full-text audit complete; practitioner interview sample, recruitment, usability themes, temporal scope, and validity threats checked
venue_year_verified: arXiv v6 dated 2026-04-14; publication metadata not separately verified
evidence_note: 17 experienced practitioners; interviews Nov. 2023–Feb. 2024, with reported saturation around interview 12; participant 18 excluded. Reports usability/adoption mechanisms and barriers (integration, enterprise/regulatory, transparency-log privacy, rate/latency, offline/air-gapped fit), not incident reduction or adoption prevalence. Recruitment network and expert/Sigstore bias limit generalization.

title: Securing the AI Supply Chain: What Can We Learn From Developer-Reported Security Issues and Solutions of AI Projects?
review_status: full-text audit complete; exact v2 headline counts, training/test distinction, thematic sample, coding procedure, and validity scope checked; compared with v1 abstract/version history
sections_checked: classifier metrics and predicted corpus construction
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2026-01-09; accepted to ICSE 2026 per arXiv comments
evidence_note: Pipeline yields 312,868 discussions and thematic coding of 753 yields 32 issue/24 solution categories. The manual classifier corpus is 723 records; separate test set is 100 keyword-free records (18 positive), so MCC=.79 does not independently validate every inferred record. Taxonomy maps developer reports; it is not incident prevalence or causal mitigation evidence. v1/v2 abstract headline counts match.

title: Does Order Matter? An Empirical Investigation into the Impact of File Ordering on Code Review Effectiveness
review_status: full-text audit complete; corpus/inclusion, bug-fix proxy, effect sizes, comment proxy, and construct/internal/external validity checked
sections_checked: threats to validity, future work, and conclusion
evidence_note: 330,343 multi-file merged PRs/756,814 file instances from 182 GitHub projects. Later-position proxy rates 56.7%→61.5%, with small associations (Pearson r=.022, Spearman rho=.018, Cramer's V=.062). Commit-message classifier validation does not validate causal attribution of subsequent fixes. Default path order differs from actual inspection; comments do not directly measure semantic review; complexity/churn/coupling incompletely controlled.
